الكَذُوبُ and الكَذُوبَةُ (tropical:) Names of the soul. (AZ, K.) See 1. ―
-b2- صَدَقَتْهُ الكَدُوبُ, [The soul (i. e. his soul) told him truth:] the soul diverted him, or hindered him, or held him back, from an undertaking, causing him to imagine himself unable to prosecute it. (TA.) One says so of a man who threatens another, and then belies himself, and is cowardly and weak. (AA.) Fr cites this hemistich: “حَتَّى إِذَا مَا صَدَقَتْهُ كُذُبُهْ
” Until, when his souls told him the truth, or diverted him, &c.: the poet assigning souls to the person spoken of because of the several opinions of the soul. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
